new_scholarship.description: The ANU International Achievement Award is a tuition fee reduction offered by The Australian National University to international students. ANU states that it 'may offer a number of awards known as the ANU International Achievement Award' and that the objective of the award is 'to attract a diverse range of academically capable overseas students to enrol in undergraduate and postgraduate coursework programs offered by the University'. Funding for the award is provided by ANU itself. There is no separate scholarship application: all eligible overseas students who have applied for admission, including those who have already accepted their offer of admission, are automatically considered, and the award reduces tuition by 20%, 25% or 50% for the duration of the program up to a maximum of four years.
new_scholarship.best_fit: An international student applying directly to ANU for admission to an undergraduate Bachelor degree, with a Selection Rank of 85 or above (or a Pacific Region citizen meeting the minimum program entry requirement), resident outside China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, the Republic of Korea and the DPRK, holding no external sponsorship toward ANU tuition, and wanting a multi-year tuition reduction of 20%, 25% or 50% with no separate scholarship application, essay, reference or interview.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Open to international students, defined by ANU as a citizen of another country not living in Australia on a permanent or humanitarian visa. The applicant must be a new commencing student, or a continuing student with an offer of admission to a higher AQF level. Residential status must be in a country not listed as eligible for the ANU Vice-Chancellor's International Achievement Award, which excludes residents of China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR and Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, the Republic of Korea and the DPRK. Undergraduate applicants must meet a Selection Rank of 85 or above (or equivalent as determined by the University) or the minimum program entry requirement for citizens of a Pacific Region country. The applicant must not receive an external sponsorship covering all or part of ANU tuition, and must accept that the award can be offered only once at each level of study, with exceptions only for progression from an undergraduate degree to a one-year Honours program or a packaged offer. Selection bases are Academic merit only; study levels covered are Undergraduate/Bachelor, Honours, Postgraduate/Masters and Graduate certificate; field of study is any eligible program except the Doctor of Medicine and Surgery (MChD) and the Master of Digital Transformation and Entrepreneurship (MDTE). No English language requirement, age limit or work-experience requirement is published on the award page.

alerts.message: If you are resident in China (including Taiwan, Hong Kong SAR or Macau SAR), Japan, Mongolia, the Republic of Korea or the DPRK, you are not eligible for the ANU International Achievement Award. The award page states residents of these countries 'may be eligible to apply for the ANU Vice-Chancellor's International Achievement Award.' Check the list of countries eligible for that award on the ANU Scholarships website before applying.

Do not wait for a scholarship application to open. There is no separate scholarship application and no scholarship deadline. The award is considered automatically as soon as you have applied for admission to ANU, including if you have already accepted your offer of admission.

alerts.trigger: Value is a percentage, not a cash amount
alerts.message: This award reduces tuition by 20%, 25% or 50%. It does not pay cash, cover living costs, travel or health cover. ANU states 'The value of the Award is stated in the letter of offer,' so the exact percentage is confirmed in your offer letter rather than on the website.

The award can be offered only once at each level of study, with exceptions only for progression from an undergraduate degree (AQF Level 7) to a one-year Honours program (AQF Level 8) or a packaged offer. Plan your AQF pathway before you take up the award, because a later re-application at the same level will not be eligible.
If you hold external sponsorship that covers all or part of your ANU tuition fees, you are not eligible for this award. Check your sponsorship terms before relying on the award in your budget.

unverified_or_removed_claims: SUBSTITUTION - the assigned target is out of scope for a bachelor's database and a different Australia award has been substituted. The assigned target was 'Australia Awards Singapore' and 'Australia Awards Brunei'. The official Singapore intake document states that 'Australia Awards scholarships will provide citizens of Singapore with the opportunity to obtain a postgraduate qualification', that awards will be offered for Semester 1 and Semester 2 2027 for 'PhD; or Masters by coursework or research', and that 'Eligible Singaporeans can apply for postgraduate study'. The official Brunei intake document states that awards 'will be offered for commencement in 2027 at either: PhD; or Master by coursework or research.' Both country profiles additionally require that applicants 'already hold an undergraduate degree'. Neither sub-programme funds a first bachelor's degree.

SUBSTITUTION - first chosen substitute was already taken. The parent Australia Awards Scholarships programme, which does fund Bachelor degrees under its Policy Handbook, was the first substitute considered, but research/bachelor/41-australia-awards-scholarships.json already contains a record for it with id 'australia-awards-scholarships'. Recording it again would have been a duplicate, so the ANU International Achievement Award was selected instead.

SUBSTITUTION DEVIATION FROM PART G. The contract's PART G guidance is to substitute 'a different row from ASSIGNMENTS.md that you have not claimed'. The ANU International Achievement Award is not a row in ASSIGNMENTS.md or ASSIGNMENTS.json, which contain no Australia Awards, Brunei or ANU rows. The operating task instruction instead directs substitution of 'ONE alternative non-excluded Australia bachelor's scholarship', which this satisfies: host region Australia, published study level Undergraduate/Bachelor, not on the RESEARCH_PROTOCOL do-not-duplicate list, and not already recorded in research/bachelor/. The deviation is recorded here rather than left implicit.

NAME CHANGE - the previously published ANU Chancellor's International Scholarship no longer resolves. The URL https://www.anu.edu.au/study/scholarships/chancellors-international-scholarship returns HTTP 404 on the ANU site. The currently published ANU tuition-reduction award for international students is the ANU International Achievement Award, which is what is recorded here. No official ANU page stating that the Chancellor's International Scholarship was renamed into this award was read, so no legacy title is asserted and no claim of continuity is made.

NO SCHOLARSHIP DEADLINE - the official page publishes no closing date, no round and no cutoff. It states 'Application period: Open for applications. Application period is open all year round.' new_scholarship.deadline_date is therefore null and deadline_precision is 'ongoing', and programme_detail_official.deadline_central is null. No calendar date has been invented. The operative deadline is ANU's admissions deadline for the intended intake, which is published separately and was not fetched.

NO DOCUMENTS - the award page prescribes no document set, no essay, no reference and no interview for the scholarship itself, because there is no scholarship application. requirements, documents and required_documents therefore describe the ANU admission application rather than a document checklist. This is a property of the award, not a research gap.

NO ENGLISH REQUIREMENT - the official award page publishes no English language requirement, no test scores and no medium-of-instruction rule. english_requirement is null and english_requirement_note records the absence. ANU admissions English requirements apply separately and were not fetched.

What I tried: (1) the official award page at study.anu.edu.au/scholarships/find-scholarship/anu-international-achievement-award - it declares no og:image, no twitter:image meta and no schema.org logo, and its only is a generic banner at imagedepot.anu.edu.au/isfs/microsite/scholarships/scholar-default1.png with alt 'hero-banner', which is a placeholder image, not a brand mark; (2) /favicon.ico, /apple-touch-icon.png and link rel=icon on the award page - the only icon link points to d3gu8jtw4r0om.cloudfront.net/files/favicon.ico, a CDN host; (3) the ANU university home page at www.anu.edu.au - it also declares only a CloudFront favicon (d1zkbwgd2iyy9p.cloudfront.net/themes/custom/webstyle/favicon.ico) and its images are content photographs (home-undergrad.jpg, home-postgrad.jpg, home-international.jpg, newsroom photos), not a logo. Why null: the only genuine ANU brand file located is https://d1blp3aor2iuhp.cloudfront.net/images/logos/logo-ANU-black.svg, which I verified live returns HTTP 200 with content-type image/svg+xml and a 16,752-byte Adobe Illustrator SVG export body, and which the repository already registers in backend/config/official_logo_overrides.json under host 'study.anu.edu.au' with official_host true and host_evidence 'cdn_on_behalf_of_host'. It is not recorded because it is served from a CloudFront hostname rather than from an anu.edu.au path, which the contract's PART D hard-ban list names as a CDN mirror and which the repo's own validator rejects (LOGO_BANNED_HOSTS includes 'cloudfront'). ANU publishes no raster logo on an anu.edu.au path anywhere I checked, so there is no compliant alternative. Null is recorded as the honest outcome.

substitution.assigned_target: Australia Awards Singapore and Australia Awards Brunei
substitution.reason: Both assigned sub-programmes are postgraduate-only. The official Singapore 2027 intake document states the award provides 'the opportunity to obtain a postgraduate qualification', is offered for 'PhD; or Masters by coursework or research', and that 'Eligible Singaporeans can apply for postgraduate study'. The official Brunei 2027 intake document states awards 'will be offered for commencement in 2027 at either: PhD; or Master by coursework or research.' Both country profiles additionally require that applicants 'already hold an undergraduate degree'. Neither funds a first bachelor's degree, so both are excluded from a bachelor's-level database.

research_notes.degree_level_confirmed: Confirmed from the official award page, which lists 'Study level: Undergraduate/Bachelor, Honours, Postgraduate/Masters, and Graduate certificate' and an award line named 'ANU International Achievement Award - Undergraduate' at 20%. The undergraduate stream's academic threshold is published as 'a Selection Rank of 85 (or equivalent as determined by the University) or above, or the minimum program entry requirement for applicants who are citizens of a Pacific Region country'. The award is not bachelor-exclusive - the same award also covers Honours, Postgraduate/Masters and Graduate certificate - so it is recorded under degree 'Bachelor's' because it applies to undergraduate study, with that wider coverage stated in new_scholarship, programme_detail_official.degree_levels and this note. The assigned target's own degree level was also checked and is postgraduate-only, which is the basis for the substitution.
